Peak Retail Corp - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Peak Retail Corp Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Peak Retail Corp's results for the second quarter of fiscal 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Merchandising Officer; and Riley Morgan, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Emily. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report Peak Retail Corp's performance for Q2 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: Comparable store sales grew 2.1% for the quarter, our third straight quarter of positive comps in a tough macro backdrop, driven by a mix of stabilizing traffic and strong ticket growth amid industry-wide softness.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Our omnichannel efforts, including BOPIS at 18% of transactions and ship-from-store supporting 25% of online orders, are fueling incremental store visits and lifting overall sales.

3. Store Performance: Remodeled locations are outperforming with 17% sales lifts, enhanced by layout optimizations, tech integrations, and experiential zones that boost dwell time and conversion.

4. Marketing Initiatives: We're shifting spend toward digital and high-ROI channels like CTV and retail media, delivering strong ROAS while driving traffic and ticket in key markets.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: Efficiencies from automation, nearshoring, and shrink reductions are supporting margin expansion, even as we navigate freight normalization and input costs.

6. Loyalty Program Update: Peak Perks 2.0 with 28 million members is enhancing personalization, bundling, and repeat visits, contributing to ticket acceleration.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more details on our financial results.

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for Q2 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.42 billion, a 2.8% increase compared to the same period last year, reflecting positive comps of 2.1% and contributions from new stores.

Gross margin was 38.2%, primarily driven by supply chain efficiencies, private label mix shift, and a 30 basis point improvement in shrink control.

Operating expenses were $642 million, representing 26.5% of revenue, benefiting from labor productivity gains and G&A leverage.

Net income was $162 million, or $0.92 per share.

We generated $275 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory levels are currently lean at 13 weeks of supply, down from 16 weeks last year, supporting strong sell-throughs.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

To give everyone more context on the drivers behind these results, let me start with our traffic versus ticket breakdown analysis, a core element of our comps performance. As a leading brick-and-mortar retailer with over 1,200 stores across apparel, home essentials, and seasonal merchandise in the value-to-mid-tier segment—competing with peers like Kohl's, Macy's, and TJX—our comps formula boils down to traffic times ticket, where ticket incorporates conversion, average unit retail, or AUR, and units per transaction. This helps us pinpoint if growth stems from volume or value, guiding our store tweaks, merchandising, and omnichannel plays.

Traffic fell 1.4% year-over-year, mirroring broader retail softness as shoppers shift to Amazon and Walmart online or cut trips due to high gas and inflation. But ticket rose a healthy 3.6% to $48.72 from $47.01, with conversion steady at 28.5%, AUR up 1.2% to $22.45 via price-pack changes, and units per transaction climbing 2.3% from checkout bundles. This mix delivered our 2.1% comps, beating the Placer.ai index's -2.8% industry drop and Macy's -1.8% traffic decline.

Sequentially, traffic improved from Q1's -2.1% to -1.4%, with mid-May inflections showing +0.8% weekly gains in June, linked to Peak Perks relaunches and curbside pickup. Ticket accelerated to a 13-quarter high of +3.6% from Q1's +2.9%, with core growth ex-inflation at +1.8%, echoing Target's strategy.

Regionally, Sunbelt stores—32% of our footprint in Southeast, Texas, and Florida—saw traffic +1.2% and ticket +4.1% to $51.23, yielding +5.4% comps amid +1.5% population growth per Census data. Midwest traffic dipped -0.9% but ticket +3.2%; Northeast urban areas faced -3.7% traffic from WFH and transit drops, offset by +4.8% ticket; West Coast -2.3% traffic but BOPIS at 18% lifted conversion. Canadian stores posted +2.4% comps.

By category, apparel (42% of sales) had -2.6% traffic but flat comps via denim refresh; home essentials (35%) +4.5% comps on bundling; seasonal (23%) +4.9% from grilling and garden expansions.

Tech plays include omnichannel synergies, PeakAI personalization in 40% of stores boosting ticket +7% for members, store cluster optimizations like garden bays lifting traffic +3.2%, and loyalty enhancements. These capex-light efforts scale to 60% by Q4.

Structurally, we're balancing traffic stabilization through local real estate and omnichannel with ticket growth via private labels at 32% of sales. Q3 comps guide +1.5-3.0%, traffic -1.0% to flat, ticket +2.5-4.0%, toward 3-5% annual growth long-term.

Next, on store remodel and renovation plans, which tie directly into our store performance. In this dynamic landscape with e-commerce pressures and post-COVID experiential shifts, our program is central to the "Stores First" approach, aiming for comps growth, productivity gains, and defending our physical edge.

We've invested $1.2 billion over three years, with $450 million for FY2024 at 4.2% of sales, matching Home Depot and Lowe's. Completed 285 remodels (24% of fleet), with 180 more in Q3-Q4, targeting 400 by year-end, up from 120 in 2023 as supply eased.

Impact: +17% two-year stacked comps lift, +12 points over non-remodeled; conversion +8-10%, dwell +22%, shrink -15% via LP tech; EBITDA +250 bps post-remodel, 18-24 month payback at 20% IRR.

Elements: 20-25% space to high-margin kitchen/bath; +5,000 sq ft boosting sales/sq ft from $650 to $780; BOPIS lockers, RFID planograms, self-checkout at 70% transactions cutting labor 12%; AR mirrors +14% add-ons; LED lighting, recycled fixtures, EV chargers per 68% eco-demand; live demos and workshops.

Sunbelt remodels (45% of 350 stores) +22% uplift; Northeast +12% with BOPIS traffic +35%; Midwest rural +9%. This reclaims share in $800B home goods, creating destinations vs. Wayfair. Next-gen pilots with AI shelving show +25% productivity. Financed by $650M FCF, debt/EBITDA 2.1x.

Turning to marketing and advertising expense trends, a key lever for traffic. Expenses hit $248 million in Q2, +12% YoY, or 4.2% of sales (+20 bps), focused on ROI amid soft appliance traffic (+1.8% comps ex-new stores).

Traditional media 28% ($69M, -10% YoY) optimized with geo-fenced OOH at 3x traffic lift. Digital 62% ($154M, +22%), search/social 45% at 8.2x ROAS; CTV $32M +35% with +28% AOV; AI DSP cut CPMs 18%; retail media $42M +55% via beacons at 4.5x ROAS for partners.

Influencers 10% ($25M, +40%), TikTok driving 1.2M downloads, 22% to BOPIS (now 28%). U.S. +14% spend, Sunbelt hyper-local +8% traffic per Placer.ai; Canada +8%, bilingual +30% engagement; Mexico pilots +25%.

CAC -11% to $28, LTV +16% to $1,240; repeat visits +14%. Q3 spend +10-12% to $260-265M, digital 65%+, AR/VR pilots, expense/sales 4.1-4.3%.

On gross margin details, particularly shrink and theft impact: Q2 gross margin 38.2% included a 10 bps YoY gain, with underlying +35 bps ex-shrink drag from private labels at 32%. Shrink at 1.75% of sales (-30 bps YoY, $28M recovered, 8 bps margin lift), vs. industry's 1.6%; theft 65% of total.

At $2.42B revenue, 1% shrink = $24M loss, high in electronics, beauty, impulse. Post-COVID spikes from ORC, booster bags +15%, sweethearting +20 bps. Urban Northeast/West 2.3%, Sunbelt/Midwest 1.4%.

Initiatives: $75M LP capex; AI vision in 650 stores (92% detection, -18% shrink); RFID 100% high-risk SKUs (-40 bps apparel); Trigo self-checkout (-60% sweethearting); ORC task force (120 convictions, $4.2M recovered). 2.5x ROI, FY shrink 1.65%, target sub-1.4% FY26.

Before outlook, key assumptions underlying our guidance: FY2024 revenue $9.75-9.85B (+3-4%), comps 2.8-3.2%, adj EPS $3.45-3.55 (+5%), gross margin +40-60 bps to 38.5%, op income +6-10%, SG&A leverage 100-150 bps.

Macro: GDP 1.8-2.2%, confidence 70-75, CPI 2.5%, unemployment 4.1-4.3%; retail sales +2.5-3%, B&M 55% share. Comps: traffic 1.5-2.5%, ticket 0.5-1.5%; Store of Future +25% dwell; BOPIS 32%; Q4 holiday 3-5%; Sunbelt +5-7%.

Margin: freight -20%, DC RFID shrink 1.2%, private label 28%; pricing +2-3%. SG&A 26.5-27%: labor +3.5%, AI scheduling -12% OT, marketing ROAS +25%, G&A -30 bps. Capex $450-500M, FCF $600-700M, debt/EBITDA 2.0x.

Phygital focus, risks recession/comps -50 bps, supply snarls.

Q4 outlook: sales $2.45-2.50B (+3-4%), comps 2.5-3.5%, margin +40-60 bps to 38.2%, SG&A 25.8-26.2%, op income $220-240M, EPS $0.85-0.95. FY2025 sales $10.1-10.3B (+3-5%), comps 3-4%, toward 7-8% op margins. Omnichannel 35% BOPIS/digital 22%, Sunbelt strength, capex $450M (120 remodels/40 new), risks housing/tariffs, upside private label/M&A.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Taylor Brooks, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to Riley Morgan to discuss store operations.

Taylor Brooks, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we launched our expanded private label sustainable home essentials line, including eco-friendly kitchen textiles and bundling options with air fryers, which has seen strong sell-through rates exceeding 12% above plan in Sunbelt markets and contributed to home category comps of +4.5%. We're excited about the potential of this new assortment and other upcoming launches like premium denim partnerships.

Riley Morgan, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Taylor. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented experiential zones and BOPIS lockers in remodeled units, along with AI personalization pilots, and are seeing positive results with traffic lifts of up to 3.2% and conversion gains in early locations.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a headwind, particularly pressuring traffic as consumers consolidate trips and trade to dollar channels—about 15% of our basket analysis shows that shift. But our ticket growth of +3.6% held firm through price-pack architecture, private label at higher margins, and bundling, allowing us to outperform on comps at +2.1%. We're passing through modest 2-3% hikes on commodities with 80% capture, and stress-tested guidance assumes CPI at 2.5% by Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Good question, Maria. For Q3, we're guiding comps to +1.5-3.0%, with traffic stabilizing at -1.0% to flat and ticket +2.5-4.0%. This embeds back-to-school strength, Sunbelt outperformance at +5%, and omnichannel lifts from BOPIS at 32% penetration, conservative on Northeast softness.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, David. We've normalized ocean freight 20% below 2022 peaks, automated our Memphis DC with 95% RFID accuracy cutting shrink to 1.2% and costs 15%, nearshored to Vietnam/India/Mexico at 60% of sourcing hedging tariffs, and cut transit 12 days. Markdown optimization via AI dynamic pricing adds $15M annualized, supporting Q4 margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Peak Perks 2.0, with 28 million members at 65% penetration—or 45 million for Haven Rewards context—is a game-changer, driving +4.5% ticket for enrollees via personalized app coupons, geo-fenced add-ons, and 55% of sales at higher margins. It contributed to conversion stability and repeat rates +14%, much like Ulta's model, scaling to loyalty-driven comps upside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Evans with Citi. Please go ahead.

Chris Evans (Citi):
On shrink, how sustainable is the improvement?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Great point, Chris. The 30 bps YoY drop to 1.75% from AI vision in 55% of stores, RFID on high-risk items, optimized self-checkout, and ORC partnerships is sustainable, with 2.5x ROI and FY guide at 1.65%. We're ahead of peers, targeting sub-1.4% by FY26 as tech densifies.

Operator:
Our final question from Lisa Wong with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Deutsche Bank):
Thoughts on marketing efficiency into holidays?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Lisa. Q3 spend up 10-12% skewed digital 65%+, with CTV ROAS 8.2x, retail media to $200M run-rate, and influencers for BOPIS. CAC down 11%, LTV up 16%, positioning for Q4 holiday comps 3-5% via measurable traffic-to-ticket lifts.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
